audit.summary: A core separation proof uses unsupported minimization and invalid lower-Gronwall inference; explicit quadratic-shear counterexamples refute the stated growing-kernel domain of Theorems 2.1 and 2.3; two local Stokes formulas require correction. No counterexample to the physical Oseen limit theorem is claimed.
limitations: Limitations: External Stokes/extension/reflections results not independently reproved
Limitations: Rotational R^2 initial-error refinement not fully verified; no admissible counterexample established
Limitations: Finite-q local-fluid interpolations and finite-q p=infinity endpoint not completely reconstructed
Limitations: No author code or particle simulation executed

Invalid minimum-distance inference — Counterevidence: Full damped relative ODE contains additional structure; a cone comparison works given uniform L<=6*pi*gamma*lambda/4, not established by H4 and displayed initial-layer estimates.

False growing-kernel domain of Theorems 2.1 and 2.3 — Counterevidence: The physical Oseen kernel alpha=1 is excluded from this counterexample. Imposing nonnegative alpha excludes mechanism but changes stated domain.

Auxiliary Stokes fields violate boundary or PDE conditions — Counterevidence: Correct weak solutions independently defined; Section3 uses plus sign; decay/scaling estimates unchanged by verified field corrections.

P1 — Counterevidence: These scalar functions are diagnostics of the inference, not particle solutions satisfying H1-H4. The full damped relative ODE contains information absent from the scalar inequality. No counterexample to the physical Theorem1.1 is established.

P2 — Counterevidence: This example uses alpha=-2 and unbounded second moments in a vanishing outlier mass. Neither a nonnegative-alpha restriction nor a second-moment hypothesis occurs in the stated general theorem. It does not refute the physical Oseen alpha=1 theorem.

P3 — Counterevidence: The weak Stokes solutions are defined independently, and the correct plus formula is already available in Section3. These local mistakes alone do not disprove the resistance estimates or the physical limit.
The finding applies to the exact reviewed source version and inspected scope; uninspected publication versions are not adjudicated.
The report retains counterevidence and unresolved questions. Publication does not repeat scientific review.
Independent human scientific adjudication remains pending; author adoption has not been requested.

proposition.claim:
The physical theorem assumes \(\gamma_N=NR\) bounded above and below, \(q>3\), convergence of the initial empirical measure in \(\mathcal W_2\) coupled to the minimum distance as in (H2), the initial relative-velocity condition \[|V_i^0-V_j^0|\le 3\pi\gamma_N\lambda_N |X_i^0-X_j^0|,\] and the energy/maximum-velocity bound (H4). In particular (H2) forces \(\lambda_N\to\infty\). The continuum comparison uses \(\gamma_N\), rather than a fixed limiting value, so omission of a separate \(\gamma_N-\gamma_\ast\) error is intentional.

With the unnormalized Euclidean norm, \(|\bar g|=\sqrt N\), the equilibrium velocity is \(\widetilde V=\mathcal R^{-1}\bar g/N\). For \(E=|V-\widetilde V|^2/(2N)\), direct differentiation gives the dissipative coefficient \(\lambda_N N c_{\mathcal R}\). Under the bootstrap estimates \(c_{\mathcal R}\gtrsim N^{-1}\) and \(\|\nabla\mathcal R^{-1}\bar g\|\lesssim N\), Proposition 3.1 yields a normalized velocity error of order \[N^{-1/2}|V-\widetilde V|(0)e^{-c\lambda_Nt}
       +\min\{t,\lambda_N^{-1}\}.\] Its time integral has the order used in (3.37)–(3.41). The extra square on a gradient norm in one intermediate display of the proof is not needed: integrating the preceding differential inequality gives the stated linear dependence directly. It is not treated as an additional substantive problem.

The variational resistance scaling \(c_{\mathcal R}\gtrsim R/(1+RS_1)\), \(C_{\mathcal R}\lesssim R\), and the powers in the force-average errors are consistent after the local field corrections below. The finite-\(p\) interpolation exponents in Lemma 2.4 were checked on their stated domain \(0<\beta<d\), \(q>d/(d-\beta)\). These checks do not remove the separation gap.

Equation reference: eq:lower. Lemma 3.4, (3.18), p. 26, claims \[
 d_{\min}(t)\ge \tfrac12d_{\min}(0)
 -C\int_0^t d_{\min}(s)A(s)\,ds,
 \quad A=|F|_\infty S_2+R^3S_2S_6^{1/2}|F|_2.\] Its proof ends on p. 44 after (5.16). On p. 29, Step 3 substitutes the force bounds into [eq:lower] (#eq:lower) and invokes Gronwall to infer (3.44), an \(N\)-uniform exponential lower bound. Step 4, p. 30, explicitly uses (3.44) in (3.45)–(3.46) to close the bootstrap for every fixed time interval. This is a direct dependency of the proof of Theorem 1.1, including its separation conclusion (1.11).

 \operatorname{div}K=0,\qquad \alpha<d-1,\] and imposes no lower bound on \(\alpha\), no uniform support bound, and no higher-moment condition beyond the selected Wasserstein distance. Under (2.3), it asserts \(\mathcal W_p(\sigma_N(t),\sigma(t))\le e^{Ct}\mathcal W_p(\sigma_N(0),\sigma^0)\). Theorem 2.3, pp. 14–15, inherits this kernel domain and asserts the corresponding vanishing-inertia estimate under (D1)–(D3).
